record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For the multi-server M/G/k queue when job sizes are not known a priori and the Gittins rank policy is extended to run the k jobs with lowest Gittins ranks, is Gittins-k optimal outside of heavy traffic?

evidence.quote: Proving the optimality of Gittins-k outside of heavy traffic remains an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an M/G/k queue: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$ to a system with $k$ identical servers (each of unit speed), and job sizes (service requirements) are i.i.d. samples from a general distribution $S$ with finite mean, so that the system load is $\rho = \lambda \mathbb{E}[S]/k < 1$. Job sizes are not known to the scheduler a priori; instead, for each job in the system, the scheduler observes only the amount of service the job has received so far (its attained service / age). 

For a job of age $a$, define its Gittins rank as
$$ \mathrm{rank}(a) \;=\; \inf_{\Delta > 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}[\min(S-a, \Delta) \mid S > a]}{\mathbb{P}(S - a \le \Delta \mid S > a)}, $$
i.e. the smallest possible ratio of expected additional service to probability of completion within an additional service quantum. The Gittins-$k$ policy is the preemptive scheduling rule that, at every moment, serves the (up to) $k$ jobs in the system whose current Gittins ranks are smallest, one on each server.

Question: Is the Gittins-$k$ policy optimal for minimizing the mean response time (expected sojourn time) in the M/G/k queue with unknown job sizes for all loads $\rho \in (0,1)$, and not merely in the heavy-traffic limit $\rho \to 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Gittins-k has been proven asymptotically optimal for mean response time in the M/G/k under heavy traffic (Scully, Grosof, and Harchol-Balter, 2020; Grosof's 2023 thesis), but its optimality outside the heavy-traffic regime remains an open question. Even existence of an optimal policy for the M/G/k with unknown job sizes in general load conditions is not established.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Multiserver Scheduling with Unknown Job Sizes in Heavy Traffic
status_evidence.snippet: M-Gittins minimizes mean response time in the heavy-traffic M/G/k... most general optimality results to date for the M/G/k with unknown job sizes.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality of Gittins-k variants is only established in heavy traffic.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Scheduling in Multiserver Queues (Grosof thesis, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: In the single-server case the optimal policy is Gittins, but it is not known whether Gittins or any other policy is optimal in the multiserver case.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality of Gittins-k outside heavy traffic remains unresolved.
